messages.subject: Re: File uploads on Shiny Server now working
messages.subject_clean: File uploads on Shiny Server now working
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

I am trying to make a simple app that lets a user upload some data to be subsetted and manipulated, etc, and then download the final product. So far I have not been able to get the data to upload in a way that will allow me to manipulate it.  When I upload data locally using either a file pathway or read.csv(file.choose()) everything works fine, so it is just a matter of getting the data to upload through glimmer.  Any help would be appreciated!  Here is a simplified version of what I am trying to do (and one version (of many) of what I have tried so far).  Thanks in advance! Pardon my ignorance, I have only been fiddling with shiny for a couple of days so far.

Cheers,

Zak

ui.R
# define the sidebar
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  # title
  headerPanel("Zak's RMBL bee label maker"),

  sidebarPanel(

    fileInput('file1', 'Choose CSV File',

              accept=c('text/csv', 'text/comma-separated-values,text/plain')),
    tags$hr(),
    downloadButton('downloadData', 'Download labels')
  ),

  mainPanel(
    tableOutput('table')
  )

))

server.R
# Define server logic
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  # get the data

  d <- input$file1

  l<-matrix(nrow=(ceiling(length(d[,1])/11))*6,ncol=11) # make the empty matrix
  k<-1 # counter in the nested for loops below

  # make the insect labels from uploaded raw data
  for (j in ((c(1:(length(l[,1])/6))*6)-5)){
    for (i in c(1:11)) {
      l[j,i]<-paste(d[k,9],"  USA: CO: Gunnison Co.")# bee number, county info
      l[j+1,i]<-paste("RMBL,",d[k,5],d[k,6]) #site info
      l[j+3,i]<-paste(d[k,2],d[1,1],", ",d[k,12]) # date and collector
      l[j+4,i]<-paste(d[k,11],d[k,10])
      l[j+5,i]<-paste("")

#####    more guts of the insect label maker that I have omitted for the sake of simplicity in this post   #####

  if (k < length(d[,1])) k<-k+1
    }
  }

  # Show the values using an HTML table
  output$table <- renderTable({
   l
  })

  # allow the data to be downloaded
  output$downloadData <- downloadHandler(
    filename = function() { paste("bee labels", '.csv', sep='') },
    content = function(file) {
      write.csv(l, file)
    }
  )
})

messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to control the number of digits for display on a table?
messages.subject_clean: Is it possible to control the number of digits for display on a table?
messages.body_plain:
renderTable passes any extra arguments along to xtable, so I think you should be able to do something like this:

renderTable({
   # Code to generate table here
}, digits=4)

It looks like xtable only lets you control the total number of digits, and not the number of digits after the decimal point. If you need finer control, you can use sprintf() to convert it to a string with a specified format. In this example, it converts column x to a string with 3 digits after the decimal point:

df <- data.frame(x=rnorm(10), y=rnorm(10), label=letters[1:10])
df$x <- sprintf('%1.3f', df$x)

If you want to do this to all columns in the data frame, you could do something like this:

# Given a column: if numeric, convert to formatted string; otherwise, return unchanged
format_num <- function(col) {
  if (is.numeric(col))
    sprintf('%1.3f', col)
  else
    col
}

# Apply the function to each column, and convert the list output back to a data frame
as.data.frame(lapply(df, format_num))

-Winston

messages.body_plain:
Yes, we have a solution for this. You'll need to install the shiny-incubator package.

# Install devtools package if needed
install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("shiny-incubator", "rstudio")

In your ui.R, include an actionButton("save", "Save"). This will create an input whose value starts at 0, and increases by 1 each time the button is clicked.

Then in server.R, include a chunk of code like this:

observe({
  if (input$save == 0)
    return()

  isolate({
    # Read inputs and save values to database here
  })
})

The "observe" function is how you create an observer, which is described in Reactivity Overview <http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#reactivity-overview>. The "isolate" function is described in Isolation <http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#isolation>.

messages.body_plain:
Shiny 0.4.1 (I believe) introduced a feature where outputs that do not visibly appear in the page are not calculated by default. This is often desirable, e.g. when an expensive-to-compute plot is contained in a tab that is not currently selected.

You can get around this behavior by adding this line right after assigning output$accesslevel:

outputOptions(output, "accesslevel", suspendWhenHidden=FALSE)

However, I cannot explain why Harun's input-based condition does not work.

messages.subject: Re: File uploads on Shiny Server now working
messages.subject_clean: File uploads on Shiny Server now working
messages.body_plain:
All of the code between the lines "shinyServer(function(input, output) {" and "# Show the values using an HTML table", needs to be wrapped up in a reactive. You're not allowed to read things off the "input" object unless you're doing it in a chunk of reactive code.

data <- reactive({
  if (is.null(input$file1)) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  d <- read.csv(input$file1$datapath)  # read the file
  # ... process your data ...
  l
})

Because it's wrapped in "reactive()", this code will execute as often as it needs to in order to stay up-to-date with respect to the inputs it uses. You can access the calculated value (in this case, the value of "l", since that's the last expression in the reactive) from output$table's and output$downloadData's render calls by calling "data()".

Great! See basename/dirname functions.

Also just be aware that the datapath file is in the temp dir for the whole R process. So depending on what Corpus/DirSource does, you may end up with files you didn't mean to (for example if two users are using the app simultaneously).

messages.subject: [runExample() is working ; runApp() is not]
messages.subject_clean: [runExample() is working ; runApp() is not]
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

First of all, congratulations for the great Shiny package!

I am facing an issue as, while working based on the tutorial <http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#>:
I am successful while running all the provided examples through the 'runExample' command.
However, the application does not work while reproducing '01_hello' example and launching my 'own' ui.R and server.R files through the 'runApp' command
The issue seems to come from the server.R file, and I get the following error:

Listening on port 8100
Error in serverFunc(input = .createValuesReader(shinyapp$session), output = .createOutputWriter(shinyapp)) :
  could not find function "renderPlot"

Does someone already encountered the same issue? Would you have any remediation action?

Thank you in advance for your help!

Thomas

ps : for infomation my code (similar to '01_hello' example)

main file:
runApp(appDir = "shinyapp")

ui.R file:
library(shiny)

# Define UI for application that plots random distributions
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  # Application title
  headerPanel("Hello Thomas's Shiny!"),

  # Sidebar with a slider input for number of observations
  sidebarPanel(
    sliderInput("obs",
                "Number of observations:",
                min = 0,
                max = 1000,
                value = 500)
  ),

  # Show a plot of the generated distribution
  mainPanel(
    plotOutput("distPlot")
  )
))

server.R file:
library(shiny)

# Define server logic required to generate and plot a random distribution
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  # Expression that generates a plot of the distribution. The expression
  # is wrapped in a call to renderPlot to indicate that:
  #
  #  1) It is "reactive" and therefore should be automatically
  #     re-executed when inputs change
  #  2) Its output type is a plot
  #
  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({

    # generate an rnorm distribution and plot it
    dist <- rnorm(input$obs)
    hist(dist)
  })

})

messages.subject: request: general purpose adaptive throttling
messages.subject_clean: request: general purpose adaptive throttling
messages.body_plain:
Wherein I drag across an input to request a series of outputs, either a slider or a dropdown or a JS client.

shiny to provide a tagged response time.

use case:

I send requests at a default throttle of .5ms.  server either takes:

1s to complete each - wasting 50% of requests

.1s to complete each, meaning responsiveness is slow for no good reason

suggestion: for a given key, record recent response times.

key might be... input which triggered update, or output identity.

uses:

* optimise response time.
* provide mechanism to allow minimal primary response, followed by detail view if input stopped or available time
* provide selection mechanism between minimal + maximal or maximal only, based upon analysis of min/max response times and optimal latency

suggestion: reactive mechanism to partially satisfy response - minial or partial or summarised response to be automatically followed by maximal response unless new request received, in which case new minimal will be transmitted.

compare: browse through images and get low dip image each time unless user browse stops, when full res is displayed (google images, apple aperture).

-Alex

I'm stumped where to begin looking; is shiny-server doing anything special to hibernate between requests?

Thanks for any other clues,
-Aaron

messages.subject: Re: Error: Failed to load Cairo backend
messages.subject_clean: Error: Failed to load Cairo backend
messages.body_plain:
Shiny does check to see if you have the Cairo package installed when renderPlot() is called. I have no idea why it should start throwing that error, though -- I haven't seen it before. Are they using Cairo directly in their apps, or are they just using renderPlot?

In 0.4.1, it was in renderPlot:
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/v/0/4/1/R/shinywrappers.R#L86

In 0.5.0, it was moved to a separate function plotPNG, which gets called from renderPlot:
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/R/imageutils.R#L33

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: how do I upload multiple files with fileInput() ?
messages.subject_clean: how do I upload multiple files with fileInput() ?
messages.body_plain:
If you want them to upload two separate files in order, then probably the easiest/best way to do that is to include two separate fileInput fields. This will let them change the file if they get it wrong.

In general though, when you upload multiple files through fileInput, then input$file1 (in your case) will be a dataframe where each row is a different file. So to retrieve the first file's datapath it would be input$file1[[1, 'datapath']] and for the second, input$file1[[2, 'datapath']].

>     }
>   )
> })

messages.subject: Re: Shiny server installation as non-root user
messages.subject_clean: Shiny server installation as non-root user
messages.body_plain:
Shiny Server was primarily designed to let many users deploy Shiny apps on a server, with each app executing with its author's permissions (what the config docs now call "autouser" mode <http://htmlpreview.github.com/?https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/blob/master/config.html>). In order to launch processes as another user, the server process needs to be root.

With the other models of deployment, there isn't a technical reason why the server would need to run as root (unless you wanted to use ports below 1024) as long as the active user is the same as the user that is specified in the config file. But we haven't modified the code that would need to check for this condition and launch the process differently.

    dataf = melt (exprs(datas[1]),varnames = c("genes"))
    pheno = cbind(pData(datas[1]), sample = rownames(pData(datas[1])))

    # check for the input variable

ylab("Log 2 value") +
xlab("Type") +
geom_boxplot()+
opts(title=paste(gene) + theme_bw() +
opts(legend.position="none"))

    })
})

# UI.r
library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

        sidebarPanel(
textInput("genes", "Enter a gene symbol", value = "MYCN"),

        #Show a tabset that includes many plots
mainPanel(
tabsetPanel(
tabPanel("Boxplot", plotOutput("Plot")),
tabPanel("Survial", plotOutput("Survial"))
  )
)
))

I've found and fixed the problem. It appears to be specific to CentOS 6.4 in combination with RStudio. The fix is in our httpuv R package, which will see an update in the next few weeks.

In the meantime you can download this build <https://s3.amazonaws.com/rstudio-private/httpuv_1.0.5.99.tar.gz> and install it like so:

R CMD INSTALL httpuv_1.0.5.99.tar.gz

messages.body_plain:
Oh, yes, error pages attempt to load a custom font from Google Web Fonts. It's OK if this does not succeed. However, when application pages load, they use a file from http://cdn.sockjs.org which does need to succeed. We have a bug logged to move the file from cdn.sockjs.org <http://cdn.sockjs.org> into our own codebase--hopefully I will be able to get to that soon. In the meantime I can't say I have a great solution for you, sorry.

messages.subject: Re: Reactive Timers for Partial render - how?
messages.subject_clean: Reactive Timers for Partial render - how?
messages.body_plain:
Our current (simplistic) approach to this problem has been to do "debouncing" and "throttling" on the client side, on the input bindings (getRatePolicy). One work item we have is to make this setting configurable on a per-input basis, so you could increase the debounce/throttle interval if you know a particular input will trigger an expensive recalculation.

That doesn't, however, solve the issue of partial rendering/subsampling. If that's really important to you then maybe this would work:

lastKnownSliderValue <- NULL
renderPlot({
  if (!identical(input$slider, lastKnownSliderValue)) {
    lastKnownSliderValue <- input$slider
    invalidateLater(300)
    plot(input$slider*sample(100,dataset))
  } else {
    plot(input$slider*dataset)
  }
})

Could be wrapped up with an API like this:

renderPlot({
  debouncedPlot(
    300,     # millisecond threshold
    {input$slider},     # explicitly provide inputs--wrap in a list() if more than one
    {plot(input$slider*sample(100, dataset))},     # Cheap version
    {plot(input$slider*dataset)}     # Expensive version
  )
})

On Wed, Apr 3, 2013 at 9:33 PM, Alex Brown <alexb...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Suppose I have a graph which takes 2 seconds to render.
>
> Suppose I could generate a partial graph (say, take sample() of the data, or similar) which takes 0.1 seconds to render and send.
>
> If the user is dragging a picker, interactivity will be poor if the 2 second graph is called each time, but okay with 0.1 seconds.
>
> Additionally, the requests may build up as the slider is pulled around, causing a series of graphs to be displayed in turn after the slider action ends with nothing the bewildered user can do to stop it.  (rather like the slowing of time that is experienced when leaving ones keys inside the car and closing the door).
>
> I see there is a reactive timer; how might we use it in the following design?:
>
> renderGraph() {
>   if (!timerExpired) {
>     plot(input$slider*sample(100,dataset))
>     resetTimer(300*ms)
>   } else {
>     plot(input$slider*dataset)
>   }
> }
>
> So for the following inputs
>
> 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 each 100s apart, it would render the subsampled graph 5 times, and after 300ms after the last one, the renderGraph would be invalidated and the full res graph uploaded.
>
> This looks a bit like invalidateLater, except that I need to know for a given render function if the timer has been invalided or not yet, so as to decide which graph to draw, and I need to be able to reset it (and maybe clear it too).

>
> -Alex

messages.subject: Re: File uploads on Shiny Server now working
messages.subject_clean: File uploads on Shiny Server now working
messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe,

First of all, thanks for all that you're doing.  Shiny is so awesome!

I'm using the upload tutorial (http://jcheng5.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#uploads).  Initially, I was getting the same error as everyone else.  Ran the update and things were working pretty well with a small data set.  I've got a csv file with 15 columns.  I'm noticing that i get an error with anything more than about 200 rows.  The error appears in the loading progress slider bar and says "<html>
<head>
  <title>An error has occurred</title>
  <link".  The full size of the file is 754x15 and about 149 KB, which is well under the 5MB size limit.

Have you ever encountered this problem?  Any ideas on a workaround?

Thanks!
Jess

On Tuesday, March 5, 2013 3:20:00 PM UTC-7, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> Many of you have been waiting patiently for file upload improvements in Shiny, especially fixing file uploads on Shiny Server. We're pretty close now, but it involved writing a whole lot of new code so I'd like to see some beta testing before we release to CRAN.
>
> Please help us beta test by following the upgrade instructions at the end of this message.
>
> Features:
> Now works with Shiny Server! (glimmer.rstudio.com <http://glimmer.rstudio.com> is already upgraded)
> Local uploads are also much faster and more robust
> Progress is displayed during upload
> Limitations:
> (Still) not compatible with IE9 and earlier
> Uploads cannot be canceled (other than reloading the page)
> Note:
> By default, Shiny limits file upload requests to 5MB; anything larger will be rejected. You can change this limit using option(shiny.maxRequestSize = x), where x is the size in bytes; a size of -1 means any size is allowed.
> ----
>
> Instructions for upgrading a Shiny Server install:
>
> Run these commands from the shell:
>
> sudo su - -c "R -e \"install.packages('shiny', repos=c(RStudio='http://rstudio.org/_packages', CRAN='http://cran.rstudio.com'))\""
>
> sudo npm install -g https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/tarball/httpuv
>
> Then restart Shiny Server. If you're using Upstart, the command is sudo restart shiny-server
>
>
> Instructions for upgrading a non-server Shiny install:
>
> Run this command from the R console:
>
> install.packages('shiny', repos=c(RStudio='http://rstudio.org/_packages', CRAN='http://cran.rstudio.com'))
>
> Then restart your R session.
>

messages.body_plain:
You could put code like this before your call to shinyServer, i.e. at the top of server.R (see this <http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#scoping> for why it goes there):

sharedData <- reactiveValues()

Inside your shinyServer function, have this:

observe({
  if (is.null(input$file1))
    return()
  sharedData$dataset <- read.csv(input$file1$datapath, ...)
})

output$contents <- renderTable({
  sharedData$dataset
})

The "observe" means that the enclosed chunk of code will be re-executed as necessary (in this case, whenever input$file1 changes). When it executes and input$file1 is present, it will read the file and put it in the sharedData reactive values holder with the name "dataset". Then you can refer to sharedData$dataset in all of your other render calls, reactives, etc.

Note that while I believe this will work, Shiny is currently not particularly well optimized for this use case. For example, if your observe code also includes input$header, input$sep, input$quote then when a user changes one of those it will cause their session to replace the sharedData$dataset value even if theirs was not the most recent file to be uploaded. You may be able to work around this with judicious use of the "isolate" function. I definitely recommend reading all three of the "Understanding Reactivity" chapters in the tutorial <http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#reactivity-overview>.

messages.subject_clean: transition of outputs or results
messages.body_plain:
I don't think it is simply an issue of needing a progress bar. Shiny and googleVis don't seem to be playing well together (at least in the case of the gvisTable and renderGvis). You can see the (bad) behavior with the example app <http://glimmer.rstudio.com/mages/Example_2/> given by the OP. If you change the inputs repeatedly, you will eventually 'break' the app and no longer see a table displayed. It seems that it is not simply a matter of requiring additional time to recalculate the results, but rather that the table will not be displayed until the app is refreshed. I tried to replace the table for this app <http://glimmer.rstudio.com/hinkelman/ofw/> with a gvisTable (version with gvisTable is not publicly hosted), but encountered the same type of buggy behavior when changing the inputs.

On Friday, March 29, 2013 8:54:11 AM UTC-5, couch...@gmail.com wrote:
> I am developing an app with shiny googleVis. I have very big amount of data, it takes time before it does calculations so there's couple of problems I ran into.
>
> Suppose this app <http://glimmer.rstudio.com/mages/Example_2/> to be an example. You can see that it has a data printed out in the table. If you click on radio button the calculation appears and table becomes pageable.  However, you can notice that some time, after you pressed the radio button, the table remains unchanged. If you have lots of calculations this time becomes longer and sometimes it's hard to know whether your data already updated or no.
>
> So the question follows, is there any possibility to remove all outputs immediately if, for example, the slider value changes? Maybe it's possible to insert some kind of progress bar or processing bar..
>
> Thank you in advance

sudo su -

Or:

sudo su - shiny
R
(from R prompt:) install.packages("your-package-name")

messages.subject: Caching with reactive expressions
messages.subject_clean: Caching with reactive expressions
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am trying to use reactive expressions in a way to cache the output on
first run for future calls. My code:

#functions.R:
runQuery <- function(dimension) {
   #Stuff

   return(result)
}

#server.R:
source("functions.R", local=TRUE)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
   getData <- reactive({
     runQuery(input$dimension)
   })

   output$plot <- renderPlot({
     data <- getData()

     #ggplot2 stuff
   })
})

#ui.R:
<select id="dimension">
   <option value="foo.bar" selected="selected">foo.bar</option>
   <option value="baz.bbq">baz.bbq</option>
</select>

When a selection (a dimension value) is made from the UI, runQuery()
incorporates the value in its query and returns a response which is used
to plot.

What I'm experiencing is that a previously selected action is
re-executing runQuery(). My expectation was that a query which was
previously executed would have been cached given that the
input$dimension value is the same and thus preventing the trip to
runQuery() on subsequent actions.

If anyone can shed some light on this, it'd be greatly appreciated.

Thanks,

-Sarven
http://csarven.ca/#i

messages.subject: Re: Caching with reactive expressions
messages.subject_clean: Caching with reactive expressions
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sarven -

Reactive expressions will only cache the most recent values -- this is so that if you have multiple outputs (or reactive expressions) that uses getData(), it won't have to run again. However, it doesn't cache old values from previous runs. If you want to do that, you'll have to cache values yourself.

You could use the memoise package to do caching. When you pass memoise() a function, it will return another function that caches return values, based in the input.

# Create a memoized version of runif()
rr <- memoise(runif)

# First run, with input 1
rr(1)
# [1] 0.6785051

# All subsequent runs with the same input (1) return the same value, because
# it is cached
rr(1)
# [1] 0.6785051

# Input of 2 will run runif(2)
rr(2)
[1] 0.5760216 0.7925082
rr(1)
# [1] 0.6785051

Keep in mind, though, that if you use memoise, the scope where you define the memoized function matters. To use it in a Shiny app so that each session gets its own cache, define it within the shinyServer function:

shinyServer(function (input, output) {
  # Create memoized function in scope of each session
  rr <- memoise(runif)

  output$numbers <- renderText({
    rr(input$n)
  })
})

If you want it to be shared across all sessions, define it outside the shinyServer function:

# Create memoized function in scope shared across all sessions
rr <- memoise(runif)

shinyServer(function (input, output) {
  output$numbers <- renderText({
    rr(input$n)
  })
})

-Winston

Hi everyone -

We've added some new features on an experimental branch:
* Setting the values of input objects from the server
* Sending arbitrary Javascript from the server to run on the client

It's not yet merged into the master development branch, but if you are feeling brave and want to experiment with it, you can install it with:
  devtools::install_github('shiny', 'wch', 'set-input')

Please note that the API is still subject to change, and it's possible that this branch could break at any time. If you do play with it and have feedback about it works, we'd like to hear it!

Here's a demo of setting inputs:
  http://glimmer.rstudio.com/winstontest/setinput/
Code:
  https://github.com/wch/testapp/tree/master/setinput

And a demo of sending Javascript:
  http://glimmer.rstudio.com/winstontest/sendjs/
Code:
  https://github.com/wch/testapp/tree/master/sendjs

-Winston

messages.body_plain:
Hey,
i wrote a little bit of code in JS to spice up my app to allow navigating between H1 tags using the keyboard.
pretty simple stuff :

<script type="text/javascript">
// scroll between headers
i = -1
tag = "H1"
document.onkeypress=function(e){
var e = window.event || e
var x = document.getElementsByTagName(tag)
var s = String.fromCharCode(e.charCode)
if (s == 'j')  {
  i += 1
  if (i > x.length) i = 0
} else if (s == 'k') {
  i -= 1
  if (i == 0) i = x.length
}
// alert(i + " " + x[i]. innerHTML)
x[i].scrollIntoView()
}
</script>

i add this script to my shiny app like this ...
## ui.r
shinyUI(
  bootstrapPage(
  includeHTML("keyboard_scroller.js") ,
....

and i have a lot of headerpanel objects in the page.

when i load the app the scrolling is not smooth. sometimes it worked and sometimes it doesn't.
it could work for two H1 tags and then i need to scroll around with the mouse to make it work again.
when testing the script on a simple HTML page it worked smoothly.
i would appreciate any help.

Haki.

On Thursday, April 11, 2013 4:09:48 AM UTC+2, Leela Manju wrote:

You can build a website using html-ui approach:
http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#html-ui

The frontend contains the usual components you use for your frontend stack.
The backend contains server.R and the other components for controllers / routes.

The link between the frontend and server.R are the name attribute for the inputs and shiny-html-output, shiny-text-output and shiny-plot-output classes for the outputs.

Hope that helps,
Alberto

messages.subject_clean: A newbie's question
messages.body_plain:
Hello Leela.

On Thursday, April 11, 2013 7:00:15 PM UTC+2, Leela Manju wrote:
> I have been working with HtmlUI, but it is not possible to navigate to another HtmlUI page. One can build just a single webpage with htmlui and as far as i know, navigation between pages can't  be achieved. Thanks for offering me a help though.

You should build your site as usual, using the stack you prefer.

For instance, if you use a MV* approach, you need to define the controllers and routes to navigate in the app.
See, for instance, opinionated frameworks as Backbone.js or Angular.js.

Then, when a page needs to communicate with R backend, you add Shiny "components": the script (shiny.js), the names and classes for ins and outs.

Are you be able to navigate between the pages without Shiny? Use the same approach after you "shined" the pages. :)

Regards,
Alberto

If you want to be able to change the value while the app is running, you can use dynamic UI. For an example, see:

Source code at:

And the tutorial page at:

These are different meanings of "activity." Interactive mode (which has been around before Shiny) refers to the prompt (>). So, if you are playing around in the prompt and just want a quick way to see a subset of data before committing the code, then feel free to use subset. If you are committing code for production purposes, you would want use [].

Reactivity is a term shiny uses for the purposes of interaction with the UI.

messages.subject: Re: Error: evaluation nested too deeply: infinite recursion / options(expressions=)?
messages.subject_clean: Error: evaluation nested too deeply: infinite recursion / options(expressions=)?
messages.body_plain:
I was just reminded by Doug's response in another thread: within a reactive expression, using input$x in a subset() likely won't work properly, because subset uses non-standard evaluation, as mentioned in the documentation. It evaluates the filtering expression in the data frame environment, which can cause problems.

Within a reactive expression, this will cause problems:
  subset(data, x == input$x)

But this should work:
  in_x <- input$x
  subset(data, x == in_x)

For writing Shiny apps, it's probably best to use square-bracket indexing instead of subset.

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: Can R return a JSON back to the webpage
messages.subject_clean: Can R return a JSON back to the webpage
messages.body_plain:
This is definitely something that we're thinking about. In the released version of Shiny, though, there isn't a good way to do this.

We're working on some stuff right now that lays the groundwork for sending messages with arbitrary JSON data to the client. To do what you're looking for, we'll have to think a bit about how to make it possible for app authors to register handlers for the data when it's received by the client.

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: Shiny on R 2.14? (httpuv dependency)
messages.subject_clean: Shiny on R 2.14? (httpuv dependency)
messages.body_plain:
Previous versions of Shiny used the websockets package, but in the current release, it switched from websockets to httpuv -- and Shiny's version dependency wasn't updated to 2.15. I believe that httpuv actually does require 2.15, but this is something that Joe can answer for sure after he's back online next week.

-Winston

    output$Plot <- reactivePlot(function() {

      start1 = paste0(input$Year1, "-", input$Month1, "-", input$Day1)

      in_start_energy <- start_energy

      end1 = paste0(input$Year2, "-", input$Month2, "-", input$Day2)
      end_energy = as.POSIXlt(end1)

      in_end_energy <- end_energy
      shinydayenergy = shinyday[(shinyday$time>=in_start_energy) & (shinyday$time<=in_end_energy),]
      plot(shinydayenergy$time,shinydayenergy$energy)
    })

Best wishes,
Oliver

2013/4/12 Winston Chang <win...@rstudio.com>

> I was just reminded by Doug's response in another thread: within a reactive expression, using input$x in a subset() likely won't work properly, because subset uses non-standard evaluation, as mentioned in the documentation. It evaluates the filtering expression in the data frame environment, which can cause problems.
>
> Within a reactive expression, this will cause problems:

>
> But this should work:

>
>
> For writing Shiny apps, it's probably best to use square-bracket indexing instead of subset.

ui.R
--------------------------------------------------------------------
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("Stocks"),

    wellPanel(
      p(strong("Stocks")),

      checkboxInput(inputId = "stock_1", label = "RANBAXY 800"  , value = TRUE),
      checkboxInput(inputId = "stock_2", label = "RCOM    700   ", value = TRUE)

    )),

  mainPanel(

    conditionalPanel(condition = "input.stock_1",
                     br(),
                     div(plotOutput(outputId = "plot_1"))),

    conditionalPanel(condition = "input.stock_2",
                     br(),
                     div(plotOutput(outputId = "plot_2")))

  )))

server.R
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  # Make a chart for a symbol
  make_chart <- function(sym) {

    u=paste("http://www.marketcalls.in/livecharts/",sym,sep="")

    browseURL("u")
    return()

  }

  output$plot_1 <- renderPlot(  { make_chart("ranbaxy") })
  output$plot_2 <- renderPlot(  { make_chart("rcom") })

})

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

messages.subject: Re: browseURL page not displayed
messages.subject_clean: browseURL page not displayed
messages.body_plain:
Hi - browseURL won't work when you run it on the server. What it does is, when you run it in an R session on your local computer, it will open up a web browser for you. When it's run on a remote Shiny server, nothing will happen.

It looks like you're trying to open up new browser windows that point to various URLs. If that is what you're trying to do, you'll probably have to add javascript code that will open the windows.

-Winston

To do this, you'd need to remove all the try() and tryCatch() wrappers - otherwise, errors will still get intercepted by the most recent try/tryCatch.

messages.body_plain:
The function that's given as the 'content' argument to downloadHandler takes one option, 'file'. When the download button is clicked, the download handler calls that function, and it uses the file argument to tell it where is should save the output file.

I don't see a way to set the output file name from knit2html(), but you can just rename it after it's created:

  output$downloadData <- downloadHandler(
    filename ="ShinyData.html",
    content = function(file) {
      knit2html("myreport.rmd")
      file.rename("myreport.html", file)
    }
  )

(Also, you're missing a closing parenthesis in ui.r.)

-Winston

messages.body_plain:
Sorry for the delay, I have been on vacation for the past week.

There's no particular place the data would need to be stored; one common pattern is to put it in your app directory as a .csv file (or multiple CSV files). Then in your server.R file you can use the read.csv function with a relative path (e.g. if the file was "foo.csv" you would simply read.csv("foo.csv")), as the process's current directory is always set to the app directory when a Shiny application is run.

If you're not sure where in server.R you should call read.csv(), then take a look at the Scoping <http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#scoping> section of the tutorial.

If your application is not showing errors but also not showing a plot, these are two common reasons:
When generating ggplot2 plots in renderPlot(), you need to explicitly call print(). So the above would become:
print(ggplot(Molten, aes(x=time, y=value, colour = variable)) +geom_line())
Make sure you're using a current version of your browser, and if it's not Chrome, Safari, Firefox, or IE10 then let us know what it is.
For showing one graph, the other, or both, consider using tabs <http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#tabsets>. For showing the release years or not, that would just be a checkboxInput in your sidebar.

I hope that helps. If you need more detailed help, feel free to send a .zip archive of what you've currently got, either to me directly or to the list.

I want to have conditional statements in the server script. But I met a problem.
There should be two operations.
If the users choose dataset 'population', then shiny can plot population,
If the users choose dataset 'cars', then shiny can plot another dataset 'offgas'

But the error shows that character string is not in a standard unambiguous format.

Simple code in the serve is as follows.

 output$Plot <- renderPlot(function() {

    dataset <- datasetInput()
    if (input$dataset == population)
          plot(dataset)
   if (input$dataset == cars)
      plot(offgas)
 })

Hope to hear from you.

Best wishes,
Oliver

messages.subject_clean: uploaded file doesnt print
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

I'm making a shiny application to identify bee species based on wing morphology (landmarks) (http://glimmer.rstudio.com/martijn1987/zutalors/). I will give you a quick rundown how to tool should work eventually.

-Upload user wingpicture
-Choose which reference dataset you want to compare your unidentified specimen too
-Choose which listfile/labels should accompany your reference data (decide the taxonomical level on which you want to identify your specimen
-Place the landmarks on specific points on the wing (in the example you have to place them on the spikes of 1 of the stars (5 landmarks total!)
-Click identify me, the species name is displayed below the picture.

One problem we are still not able the fix is the uploading. When we run the tool locally, it sometimes does print the uploaded picture. But only if you have already uploaded it before. I think this is because the program tries to print it before the upload is finished. When I run it online I can't manage to get the uploaded picture at all, but some people seem to be able to.

Does anyone have a solution for this?

ui, server and js are here: https://gist.github.com/anonymous/5413170

> Sorry for the delay, I have been on vacation for the past week.
>
> There's no particular place the data would need to be stored; one common pattern is to put it in your app directory as a .csv file (or multiple CSV files). messages.body_plain:
Shiny Server doesn't implicitly read .RData files from inside the app directory. We've found this to be a common source of errors. However, I can see in your code that you're also explicitly defining RoseBella in server.R, so that isn't the problem.

The problem here is that in your ggplot aesthetics, you're including the dataframe:
  aes(y = RoseBella$Rosemary.Rosemary)
where only the column is needed:
  aes(y = Rosemary.Rosemary)

ggplot2 knows to evaluate the aes arguments in the context of the data argument you passed to ggplot(). I imagine you'll wonder, then, why it works when you test the code outside of Shiny. Well even though the latter code is "better", the former still ought to work, were it not for this bug in ggplot2 <https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/pull/744>.

Anyway, if you make the change above then you'll see everything start to work.

messages.subject_clean: pairs of inputSelects reactively connected update problem
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have the following problem and cannot figure out how to get around it.

What I do is very basic: First I upload a data file, the I select a few variables of it in in a selectInput widget.

Based on that selection for each variable an array of widget is presented, packed into one wellPannel(div(...)) wrapper.

The first two of those widgets are inputSelect widgets of which the first one selects one of the previously determined variables and the second one as a reactive respone presents the differen values of that selected single variable.

However, what happens is: I change the selection in the first inputSelect, then the screen updates so that the second inputSelect show the rigth values, but the first one is reseted to its default value.
As a consequence the screen updates again so that the second inputSelect switches back to its initial value aswell.

This is the current code for one variable:

        conditionalPanel("input.checkfile",
        wellPanel(
            h5("Please select the targeted proportions for each variable:"),
                div(class = "row offset1",
                conditionalPanel(n.vars() > 0,
                div(class = "span3", wellPanel(
                    selectInput("var1propselect", "Select variable:", give.varnames(), give.varnames()[1]),
                    selectInput("var1valueselect", "Select target value:",
                                as.list(give.valuelabels()[[selected.order()[1]]])),
                     sliderInput("var1propslider", "Set proportion range:",
                                    0,1,value = c(0,1),step = 0.05,animate=FALSE),
                    helpText("__________________________"),
                     selectInput("var1proplink","Link with variable (optional):",c(list("none"),give.varnames())),
                    sliderInput("var1weightslider", "Set relative weight of variable (optional):",
                                0,1,value = 1,step = 0.01,animate=FALSE))
                )),
               ...
        )

So what seems to be the problem that by updating selectInput("var1valueselect",...)  in the same moment selectInput("var1propselect",...) gets rerendered with its default value.
What I could imagine to solve the problem could be a replacement for  give.varnames()[1] that actually stores the value of the selection in selectInput("var1propselect",...) from before the whole div gets updated and sets the new default value for the widget.

Any ideas how to do this or something better?

Best,
WF

messages.subject: Re: numericInput widget arguments "min" and "max" do not show any effect
messages.subject_clean: numericInput widget arguments "min" and "max" do not show any effect
messages.body_plain:
numericInput() emits HTML code like this:
<input id="in_numeric" type="number" value="5" min="1" max="10" step="0.5"/>

The browser then decides how to handle the input. At least in the latest version of Chrome, the numeric input lets you type in any number. However, if you click on the up and down arrows, it does restrict the values that are accessible.

If it's very important to validate the values, you should make sure to do it on the server side (although it's certainly not a bad thing to also validate on the client). Validating input on the client can of course make things easier for the user, but the user can hypothetically also modify the client-side code to send any values that they want.

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: Error: su: must be run from a terminal
messages.subject_clean: Error: su: must be run from a terminal
messages.body_plain:
Despite the misleading error message, the problem here is indeed that Shiny Server expects to be run with root privileges.

This is because Shiny Server was originally designed to allow all users (or all users in a certain group) on the server to host Shiny apps themselves, and their apps would execute with their permissions. We use su to drop privileges when spawning the R process (rather than simply fork/setuid/exec), since it knows all the subtleties about doing so, e.g. which environment variables need to be dropped/changed, the right incantation to setgid/initgroups, etc.

Shiny Server still allows you to do this (it's the autouser <http://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/blob/master/config.html#overview> mode) but with the other two modes of operation, "site directory" (the default) and "direct mapping", it's easy to imagine the Shiny Server process running as a particular user and all the spawned R processes running as the same user. Other than listening on port <1024 there would be no inherent need to run as root. But Shiny Server doesn't detect that case right now.

I didn't think about the PaaS case--that is a particularly good reason for us to remove the run-as-root restriction. I'll see if I can take care of this.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe,

In case your email client ate up my email, you can see the source here:

https://groups.google.com/group/shiny-discuss/msg/1544f47c0ab777d5?dmode=source&output=gplain&noredirect

I'll elaborate:

What I'm trying to do is to have a proper URI mechanism where unique
URIs would make unique requests to the Shiny server. Plain ol' URI
rewriting.

To build on my example:

Intention is for http://example.org/foo/bar to show a scatter plot,
where foo is the x variable and bar is the y variable.

Similarly, http://example.org/foo/baz would show a scatter plot, where
foo is the x variable and baz is the y variable.

Hence, something needs to do along the lines of what Apache does:

RewriteRule ^/([^/]+)/([^/]+)$  index.php?x=foo&y=bar [L]

Although this is not the job of URI rewriting, when the query values
(i.e., x=foo, y=bar) are available to server.R, the application would be
able to auto-select form inputs (for ui.R) which corresponding to the
parameters in the URI.

I'm hoping to use the shiny server in this fashion, and not as a single
entry point application at http://example.org/ . If this is not the job
of Shiny server, I would appreciate a pointer, if any.

Thanks,

-Sarven

messages.subject: Shiny server and ui
messages.subject_clean: Shiny server and ui
messages.body_plain:
I have been making an r package that uses shiny interfaces as demos and they work great. The one problem I have is that there seems to be some hoops I have to jump through if I want more that one demo. For instance I cannot have multiple server.R and ui.R files in the demo directory. I can have multiple files called from demo that can run multiple interactive shiny demos, but they have to jump through hoops to point to the correct server and ui files. It also gets rather difficult to track multiple files with the same name. I investigated the source code and it seems the runApp() function I use calls the startApp() function. This has two lines that set the server.R and ui.R files.
uiR <- file.path.ci <http://file.path.ci>(getwd(), 'ui.R')
serverR <- file.path.ci <http://file.path.ci>(getwd(), 'server.R')
Is there a reason that these are hard-coded to these names. Would it be more robust if you could pass runApp() two arguments which would also be passed to startApp(). They could be defaulted by runApp(ui = 'ui.R', server = 'server.R') if you give it the directory, but you can then have more flexibility by being able to call runApp(appDir = 'dir') directory or runApp(ui = MY'ui.R', server = 'MYserver.R'). Or it would even open the door to using an actual function as an argument. Since server.R consists of a shinyServer() which wraps a function you could pass the function as an argument, you could have logic before hand that could modify the function based on the circumstances. This could give different interfaces based on the data or other parameters involved.

So it'd have to be an alternate communication channel.
>

> On Fri, Jan 11, 2013 at 12:19 AM, Adam Edgley <adam....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > What if you declared an output$progress_listener function returns a numeric vector? Then have a progress bar widget that listens to the output$progress_listener and update. The output$progress_listener function would be called from other reactive functions as they step through each line of code, for example:
> >
> > progress_listener = reactiveProgress(function(perc_complete){
> >    return(perc_complete)
> > }
> >
> > long_progress = reactive(function() {
> >   mydata = database_call()
> >   progress_listener(50)
> >   fit = Mclust(mydata)
> >   progress_listener(75)
> >   return(fit)

> > > Yes, in the ui.R.
> > >
> > > There's no possible way to know how much time is left. You can determine the elapsed time in pure JavaScript if you wanted to; whenever that conditionalPanel condition is evaluated, run a function. This function will see if the busy status (presence/absence of shiny-busy CSS class on <html>) has changed since the last time. If it has changed from not-busy to busy, then save the current time. Then once every second or so (using setInterval) calculate the number of seconds since the start time, and update the progress message with that value.
> > >
> > > var wasBusy = false;
> > > var elapsedTimer = null;
> > > var startTime = null;
> > > function updateBusy() {
> > >   var isBusy = $('html').hasClass('shiny-busy');
> > >   if (isBusy && !wasBusy) {
> > >     startTime = new Date().getTime();

Hi,

I just tried to install shiny server on two separate machnes running  ubuntu 12.10 and ubuntu 12.04 LTS respectively. A couple of errors popped up. First, if I understand correctly, it appears that the node - npm install instruction at: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/wiki/Ubuntu-step-by-step-install-instructions could be changed from: "sudo apt-get install nodejs npm" to "sudo apt-get install nodejs" as npm is now installed automatically as part of nodejs.

Second, both attempts at installing shiny server choked at the install node-unixgroups part of the script. messages.subject: Shiny & Reproducible Research
messages.subject_clean: Shiny & Reproducible Research
messages.body_plain:
Thank you Joe and Winston, everyone else who may be on the shiny team, as well as the rest of the contributors in this group, my project has progressed much further in one month than I had anticipated in large part due to shiny and all of your support.

My next largest concern, which I have not yet come to an elegant solution for, is a matter of reproducible research.  It all boils down to being able to track the user and be able to follow their steps to produce the same results.  The issues that have come up are 1) The code used for shiny would have to be manually altered to get rid of shiny specific functions and mechanics in order to run through as an R script (I presume?),  2) The user is likely to want to save multiple plots generated with each plot function with the shiny program, so simply using the last available reactives and inputs$s will not suffice,  3) The user inputs are not likely to be linearly performed (user goes through steps 1-7, decides to change something in step 4 and continues from that point forward again) and 4) the R history saved appears to just be the runApp() function, at least when run locally.

The practical reasons for needing reproducibility could be as simple as a collaborator comes to me and says "I made this plot yesterday with the application you made, I think I used the following criteria, could you please make it again with the following custom changes to it?" or "I made this plot a couple months ago, and I performed some independent validation and would like to publish it- could you provide the code used to produce it for the supplemental portion?"

So I figured I would check in to see if anyone else had given thought to the above, and if the shiny team had anything in the works (or even draftboard/to-do list) related to these issues.  The ugly solution I had come up with was to create a list of lists that will be appended each time an action button is clicked- named after the action button pressed and the time/date when it was pressed, including the list of input$s, reactives and their contents, and upon saving a plot, the relevant list will too be saved.  And at the end, the list of lists (stalking everything they did) would also be saved.  These could be used to be input the shiny application manually again, or an R script could be mocked up to mimic the shiny application, minus the reactives, isolates, action buttons, overlapping object names and etc, implementing the saved input$s and reactives.  I would love to hear a better solution.

Thanks again,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: Shiny & Reproducible Research
messages.subject_clean: Shiny & Reproducible Research
messages.body_plain:
I'm not sure if this helps but we had ideas for how to enhance the framework to allow for unit testing; this would involve being able to simulate inputs, and read outputs, from an R script. I guess this would help with the "playback" but not "record" part of the problem.

On Mon, Apr 22, 2013 at 11:15 AM, Mike C <parado...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Thank you Joe and Winston, everyone else who may be on the shiny team, as well as the rest of the contributors in this group, my project has progressed much further in one month than I had anticipated in large part due to shiny and all of your support.
>
> My next largest concern, which I have not yet come to an elegant solution for, is a matter of reproducible research.  It all boils down to being able to track the user and be able to follow their steps to produce the same results.  The issues that have come up are 1) The code used for shiny would have to be manually altered to get rid of shiny specific functions and mechanics in order to run through as an R script (I presume?),  2) The user is likely to want to save multiple plots generated with each plot function with the shiny program, so simply using the last available reactives and inputs$s will not suffice,  3) The user inputs are not likely to be linearly performed (user goes through steps 1-7, decides to change something in step 4 and continues from that point forward again) and 4) the R history saved appears to just be the runApp() function, at least when run locally.
>
> The practical reasons for needing reproducibility could be as simple as a collaborator comes to me and says "I made this plot yesterday with the application you made, I think I used the following criteria, could you please make it again with the following custom changes to it?" or "I made this plot a couple months ago, and I performed some independent validation and would like to publish it- could you provide the code used to produce it for the supplemental portion?"
>
> So I figured I would check in to see if anyone else had given thought to the above, and if the shiny team had anything in the works (or even draftboard/to-do list) related to these issues.  The ugly solution I had come up with was to create a list of lists that will be appended each time an action button is clicked- named after the action button pressed and the time/date when it was pressed, including the list of input$s, reactives and their contents, and upon saving a plot, the relevant list will too be saved.  And at the end, the list of lists (stalking everything they did) would also be saved.  These could be used to be input the shiny application manually again, or an R script could be mocked up to mimic the shiny application, minus the reactives, isolates, action buttons, overlapping object names and etc, implementing the saved input$s and reactives.  I would love to hear a better solution.
>
> Thanks again,
> Mike

> I'm not sure if this helps but we had ideas for how to enhance the framework to allow for unit testing; this would involve being able to simulate inputs, and read outputs, from an R script. I guess this would help with the "playback" but not "record" part of the problem.
>
> On Mon, Apr 22, 2013 at 11:15 AM, Mike C <parado...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Thank you Joe and Winston, everyone else who may be on the shiny team, as well as the rest of the contributors in this group, my project has progressed much further in one month than I had anticipated in large part due to shiny and all of your support.
> >
> > My next largest concern, which I have not yet come to an elegant solution for, is a matter of reproducible research.  It all boils down to being able to track the user and be able to follow their steps to produce the same results.  The issues that have come up are 1) The code used for shiny would have to be manually altered to get rid of shiny specific functions and mechanics in order to run through as an R script (I presume?),  2) The user is likely to want to save multiple plots generated with each plot function with the shiny program, so simply using the last available reactives and inputs$s will not suffice,  3) The user inputs are not likely to be linearly performed (user goes through steps 1-7, decides to change something in step 4 and continues from that point forward again) and 4) the R history saved appears to just be the runApp() function, at least when run locally.
> >
> > The practical reasons for needing reproducibility could be as simple as a collaborator comes to me and says "I made this plot yesterday with the application you made, I think I used the following criteria, could you please make it again with the following custom changes to it?" or "I made this plot a couple months ago, and I performed some independent validation and would like to publish it- could you provide the code used to produce it for the supplemental portion?"
> >
> > So I figured I would check in to see if anyone else had given thought to the above, and if the shiny team had anything in the works (or even draftboard/to-do list) related to these issues.  The ugly solution I had come up with was to create a list of lists that will be appended each time an action button is clicked- named after the action button pressed and the time/date when it was pressed, including the list of input$s, reactives and their contents, and upon saving a plot, the relevant list will too be saved.  And at the end, the list of lists (stalking everything they did) would also be saved.  These could be used to be input the shiny application manually again, or an R script could be mocked up to mimic the shiny application, minus the reactives, isolates, action buttons, overlapping object names and etc, implementing the saved input$s and reactives. messages.subject: Commercial Shiny Server Timeline and Features?
messages.subject_clean: Commercial Shiny Server Timeline and Features?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Shiny Devs. (Winston, Joe, etc.),

First of all, I want to to thank you for building this wonderful web framework. I've attempted to work with other frameworks in the past, and found them far more difficult to implement and use, and ultimately it was easier to just avoid them altogether. Shiny, on the other hand, has been incredibly straightforward to use and we've been able to make some powerful apps out of it already.  Notably, it's allowed me to use the analytic power of R in situations where other, more clunky, solutions were in place and create a whole lot more impact with my clients/colleagues. SO BIG KUDOS TO YOU AND THE TEAM!

For me to make full use of the software and really take it to the next level, we'll need some good and powerful authentication (all of my data is highly confidential and there's concerns in my company that web-sockets can be hacked a little easier than alternatives) and other back-end solutions to make sure the proper infrastructure is in place to share our Shiny apps outside of the intranet.

I know you have discussed elsewhere on the forum that authentication will be part of the commercial version. Are there any other features you plan to implement that you can share with us?  Would this be a proper place to make requests for the types of features we'd hope for out of the commercial version of this software? And lastly, any ideas on when you'll be offering this or when you'll start building it up beyond the beta?

Obviously you're free to leave me/us out of this (I don't want to jeopardize you making some real money off of all the work y'all have done!), but I'd--maybe others too?--certainly love to know!

Regards,
Aaron

messages.subject: Re: suppress red error messages in shiny webpage
messages.subject_clean: suppress red error messages in shiny webpage
messages.body_plain:
I recommend having your reactive functions/expressions and renderers check whether their dependencies are ready, and return NULL if not; this way, if you do have a real error later in the app, it will still be shown.

However, if you really want to hide error messages, you can do it with this CSS (add it anywhere in your page):

tags$style(type="text/css",
  ".shiny-output-error { visibility: hidden; }",
  ".shiny-output-error:before { visibility: hidden; }"
)

messages.body_plain:
I am the author of rCharts that Kenton mentioned in his post. Polychart, the JS library that is one of the many that works with rCharts, is based on grammar of graphics. In fact, the author of Polychart states that ggplot2 was her motivation when she built Polychart. I am in the process of recreating plots from the R cookbook using rCharts and Polychart and it seems like 90% of the capabilities are covered.

Interactivity is already built into Polychart and rather simple to use. However, it still requires users to know a little bit of JS/Coffeescript. With `knitr` it is easy to seamlessly integrate everything. You can see an example of this here http://ramnathv.github.io/rChartsNYT/. The third graph has interactivity added using a bit of coffeescript, which knitr makes really easy to integrate.

The only hitch is with the license of Polychart. It is not free for commercial use.

I know that rCharts is not as robust a solution as r2d3 or gg2v will turn out to be. But, I am looking for feedback so that I can take rCharts to the best of what it can do.

Ramnath

messages.subject: Re: Multiple users
messages.subject_clean: Multiple users
messages.body_plain:
Hi Taylor,

Multiple users using the same Shiny program exist in the same R process, but each user gets their own set of inputs/outputs. It's possible to make users affect each other, by creating reactive values <http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#reactivity-overview> in shared scope <http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#scoping> but this is a more advanced technique.

The 2GB memory cap is per process, and thus, per app. There are currently no CPU caps in place, but we will send you a polite email if we notice one of your apps using a CPU at 100% for hours, and kill the process if we don't hear back from you.

messages.subject: Re: pairs of inputSelects reactively connected update problem
messages.subject_clean: pairs of inputSelects reactively connected update problem
messages.body_plain:
hi,

sorry I do not have the time right now to write an example, but I solved the problem and will explain it in short:

- I had an renderUI object which was an array of widgets within a html-division
- arguments of of the different widget partially were dependent on the input-values derived from other widgets within the same division
- user input one widget "1" updated the dependend ones as intended, but causes also rerendering of the whole division resulting in setting widget "1" back to its default value, which then of course reseted the dependend widgets (pain!)

solution:

- input arguments of widget "1" for exaple has to look like:

widget("widget_input_id", "name", value.arguement = isolate(input$widget_input_id))

- I think this only works for a "value.argument" that can take the value NULL, because this is the value the "input$widget_input_id" takes before the widget actually exists

Hope it helps...
WF

messages.subject: Re: Commercial Shiny Server Timeline and Features?
messages.subject_clean: Commercial Shiny Server Timeline and Features?
messages.body_plain:
We're hoping to launch a beta version of the commercial version of Shiny Server in June. It will include authentication. With your situation I imagine you will want to run Nginx, Apache, or HAProxy in front of it to provide SSL termination <http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SSL_termination_proxy> and shut off access to the Shiny Server port at the firewall (we will also provide SSL/TLS support directly in Shiny Server, but, it is generally a best practice to put a best-of-breed web/proxy server like the aforementioned in front of your app servers as a first line of defense).

In other words, your users will connect to e.g. Nginx via HTTPS on port 443, then Nginx will hit Shiny Server on port 3838 (or on a Unix domain socket, which will be supported soon).

We are not sure when a v1 of the commercial version will come, it really depends on the feedback we get. If the beta tag is a show stopper for you, let us know.

I don't know why websockets would be more easily hacked than regular HTTP--if you have any evidence (even the flimsiest) of that I'd love to hear it! And anyway if you are running on HTTPS then the websocket is connecting over HTTPS as well.

> Hi Shiny Devs. (Winston, Joe, etc.),
>

I've attempted to work with other frameworks in the past, and found them far more difficult to implement and use, and ultimately it was easier to just avoid them altogether. Shiny, on the other hand, has been incredibly straightforward to use and we've been able to make some powerful apps out of it already.  Notably, it's allowed me to use the analytic power of R in situations where other, more clunky, solutions were in place and create a whole lot more impact with my clients/colleagues. SO BIG KUDOS TO YOU AND THE TEAM!
>
> For me to make full use of the software and really take it to the next level, we'll need some good and powerful authentication (all of my data is highly confidential and there's concerns in my company that web-sockets can be hacked a little easier than alternatives) and other back-end solutions to make sure the proper infrastructure is in place to share our Shiny apps outside of the intranet.
>
> I know you have discussed elsewhere on the forum that authentication will be part of the commercial version. Are there any other features you plan to implement that you can share with us?  Would this be a proper place to make requests for the types of features we'd hope for out of the commercial version of this software? And lastly, any ideas on when you'll be offering this or when you'll start building it up beyond the beta?
>
> Obviously you're free to leave me/us out of this (I don't want to jeopardize you making some real money off of all the work y'all have done!), but I'd--maybe others too?--certainly love to know!
>
> Regards,
> Aaron

messages.subject: Re: tabPanels not loading
messages.subject_clean: tabPanels not loading
messages.body_plain:
For the second issue, can you try this... after hiding or showing, trigger the 'shown' or 'hidden' event on that element, like this:

$('#conclusion').hide().trigger('hidden');

But it will also run into the same issue as the first problem, and that is, submitButton currently doesn't play nice with either tabsets or outputs that show/hide themselves. We're thinking of deprecating submitButton, in favor of actionButton/isolate <https://groups.google.com/d/msg/shiny-discuss/l8ZcauoOtuw/0pYyU5slVgsJ>. actionButton in the past has required the shiny-incubator package, but we've just added it to Shiny proper. It's not in the CRAN release yet but you can install it directly from GitHub with devtools::install_github("shiny", "rstudio").

So to summarize,

1) Trigger hidden/shown events when showing/hiding
2) Install latest Shiny
3) Get rid of submitButton and use actionButton + isolate instead

messages.subject_clean: Working with inputs generated in renderUI
messages.body_plain:
So I've generated a length of numericInputs in a renderUI function in server.R, and they show fine through a uiOutput in UI.R. They even pre-populate correctly with the values from the source tables.

However, I'd also like them to be reactive, so as the user changes the spinner values, they kick off the chain of dependencies for items that rely on those values. I'm having trouble with this part, in that conceptually there is a series of inputs generated in server.R, and even if I make them reactive (or so I think), they are not. Ideas welcome.

--- relevant snippet of server.R ---

require(data.table) #faster than data frames!

values <- reactiveValues()
# initialize wt here
values$wt <- wt

output$namesP <- renderUI({
dat <- indic.dt[DRI_RISK_TYPE == "PRC",list(DRI_DESCRIPTION,Indicator_ID,WEIGHT)]
  lapply(1:nrow(dat), function(i) {
   descrip <- dat[i]$DRI_DESCRIPTION
   indicator <- dat[i]$Indicator_ID
p(numericInput(inputId="Indicator",label="",min=0,max=1,step=0.1,value=getWt(indicator,values$wt)),descrip)
})
})

messages.body_plain:
Hello Ramnath

First let me congratulate you on your excellent contribution to the R community with rCharts.

Personally, i am new to javascript and web programming, but i have been trying to learn from your package in order to see how to combine javascript with shiny. I have been able to understand most of the source code on Github, but there is one aspect that confuses me a bit, and I was wondering if you can help me with it.

What i am confused about is that on Shiny Tutorial Documentation, i read about having to define "Shiny.OutputBinding" and having to "Shiny.outputBindings.register", ... etc as it's done is the following example by Alex Brown:  https://gist.github.com/anonymous/4358023 (which is a basic example of using D3 with R-Shiny)

However, i couldn't find anything similar to that in rCharts. Is it burried somewhere in the source code and i couldn't find it, or is that not included for a reason?

I would appreciate if you can reply back with an explanation that will help me learn R/Shiny + javascript integration better

Thank you

On Thursday, December 20, 2012 3:40:34 PM UTC-5, Alex Brown wrote:
> I'm an avid user of Hadley Wickham's http://ggplot2.org, and I want to use the props thus developed to build shiny apps with d3.  This question has come up a couple times on the board, and I want to share my thoughts to spark a discussion of how to make this easy.
>
> I see 4 routes to this being a reality, with different pros and cons.
>
> 1) d3 Display backend to R.
>
> Much like R can print to pdf, svg, png, cairo, add a d3 backend.  Interactivity would then have to either be automatic, or retrofitted to metadata in grid, ggplot etc.  This would be solid and widely compatible with R plot types
>
> 2) Grid to d3 converter.
>
> Probably easier to write an initial version of, a function which takes a Grid object and sends the primitives to d3.  Likely to be a bulky data format, since the same data may be carried different ways (repeated grob descriptions, implied range in scales and plots etc).  It also would be more difficult to complete since grid is large and extensible.
>
> Would work with lattice and ggplot, but not base plot
>
> 3) Ggplot_build to d3 converter
>
> Once you have declaratively specified your plot in ggplot using geoms, scales, data, stats, position, facets and aesthetics, ggplot uses ggplot_build to internally process the data structures - and creates a new object with all of the work done.
>
> This would be a neat place to intercede, although my initial pass over this wasn't as happy as I would like; the data is not truly meant to be human readable, some data is implicit or spread out, and it's possible the format will change in the future.
>
> d3 would need methods for each of the geoms, scales etc, although a small initial working set wouldn't be too hard.  Also allows more flexibility in the form of the output - d3 can do things a bit differently.
>
> Compatible with ggplot but not lattice or base.
>
> 4) Complete port of ggplot into d3.
>
> In this scheme, you essentially send the unprocessed ggplot object (or just the declaration) up to d3, and it does all the work.  That's my current approach, since it gets d3 native performance and style, plus lots of flexibility.
>
> Not really compatible with anything except my brain.
>
> ---
>
> If I get around to it I'll send some code examples.
>
> -Alex

messages.subject: Re: Initial thoughts on shiny, ggplot and d3
messages.subject_clean: Initial thoughts on shiny, ggplot and d3
messages.body_plain:
I am posting this reply here for the benefit of the group.

rCharts takes a very different approach to generating JS based charts. Essentially, everything happens within R. Every time the user changes an input, rCharts outputs a fresh set of JS code to the page. Since, everything happens within R, rCharts does not require any Shiny bindings. Note that bindings are required when you want R to talk to JS. rCharts directly generates the required JS and hence is not really talking with JS.

The page refresh is faster than generating an R plot, since we are only outputting text.

messages.body_plain:
G3plot's approach is to provide an interface using grammar of graphics but all the work is done in JavaScript.

It extends ggplot like capabilities by allowing interaction with the plot to talk to other plots and the server.

It can be used to build a web shiny application customised to your data set and r analyses without needing to learn JavaScript or d3, and very rapidly.

http://glimmer.rstudio.com/alexbbrown/g3plot/#dataSet=Indometh,tabSelected=G3Plot

Also take a look in GitHub (linked from above) and read Plots.R and PlotInputs.R.

There's no documentation right now beyond how to use it in your app.

-Alex

messages.body_plain:
g3plot look terrific, and I look forward to playing with it and learning from the code. While, we are discussing features, I thought it would be good to point out what rCharts can do.

1. It can be used straight from R, without knowing any javascript or D3. Advance customization requires JS, but not terribly complicated.
2. It is not restricted to just d3.js. It support six JS libraries so far including Polychart, which is based on Grammar of Graphics.
3. It can be used to create standalone charts, shiny apps or in a webpage/slidify deck.

So in short, rCharts attempts to produce JS visualizations from R, using an interface already familiar to R users.

I put together a short demo video, which you can see here

http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nYr5KzaR1Vc

messages.body_plain:
Hi - we're looking into how to safely update the system to R 3.0. The problem is that, if we were to update it now, everyone's apps would break, since the packages installed in R 2.15 won't load in 3.0.

The new version of devtools,1.2, requires R 3.0, but you can install the previous version with the following:

download.file('http://cran.rstudio.com/src/contrib/Archive/devtools/devtools_1.1.tar.gz',
  destfile='devtools_1.1.tar.gz')
install.packages('devtools_1.1.tar.gz', type='source', repos=NULL)
unlink('devtools_1.1.tar.gz')

-Winston

messages.subject_clean: Are reactive elements made "dirty" by changing their display size
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bob, this behavior is specific to plots, and then only if the size of the plot actually changes. One of the reactive inputs that renderPlot uses under the covers is the height and width of the corresponding plotOutput element. So when the size of the plotOutput changes, the changed dimension is sent just as any other changes input would be sent, and then a flush is performed.

Hope that clears things up.

On Saturday, April 27, 2013, Bob Anderson wrote:

> I have just begun using Shiny and noticed that if I resize the browser window such that a display element (like a plot) changes size or position, the relevant code block in server.R gets rerun, even though no reactive input in that code block has changed.  It is obvious that such behavior is required in order to enable the redrawing of the output element.  I have no problem with that.  But this situation was not mentioned in the tutorial (great BTW) section on "Execution Scheduling".
>
> My question is this: is it correct to assume that this situation is handled simply (and solely) by setting the invalidation flag of any resized reactiveOutputs followed by a "flush" ?
>

The first slider shows what happens to the averages if you change the cutting point from 90, a simple way to graphically determine if there is a tipping point, as proposed by their paper. So, I believe Shiny is going to be a very useful tool for research, in addition to showcasing it as an app.

Ramnath

> > > 1. It can be used straight from R, without knowing any javascript or D3. Advance customization requires JS, but not terribly complicated.

> > > 3. It can be used to create standalone charts, shiny apps or in a webpage/slidify deck.

> > > http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nYr5KzaR1Vc
> > >
> > >

> > > > It extends ggplot like capabilities by allowing interaction with the plot to talk to other plots and the server.
> > > >
> > > > It can be used to build a web shiny application customised to your data set and r analyses without needing to learn JavaScript or d3, and very rapidly.

messages.subject: Re: ShinyUI
messages.subject_clean: ShinyUI
messages.body_plain:
Currently either you use those 3, or you throw it all away and use bootstrapPage instead of pageWithSidebar. bootstrapPage gives you an empty body where you can use any of Bootstrap's classes (see Bootstrap's examples here <http://twitter.github.io/bootstrap/scaffolding.html>), like so:

shinyUI(bootstrapPage(
  div(class="container",
    div(class="row",
      div(class="span4",
        div(class="well", ...)
      ),
      div(class="span8", ...)
    )
  )
))

Dear Shiny folks,

I'm been working on a Shiny app that pull tweets containing a same hashtag together for some simple analysis. However, I'm experiencing some wired problem that's out of my knowledge, and I couldn't get any answer from Google either. The problem is (as you can see from the link above) the app stopped updating after April 27, even if the tweets have been growing every hour. I've checked tweet data which are automatically updated every hour, and didn't find any problem. But weirdly the application will not reflect the change of data. I wonder whether there's a way to restart an already deployed Shiny app on Glimmer. Any advice will be highly appreciated.

Thanks,
Bodong

I use a makefile to manage my Shiny apps, so that both the source on github and the app on glimmer are updated simultaneously. Here are the lines from my makefile. You need to  substitute username and repo with yours. When you do make deploy, the app will be pushed to github and to glimmer. deploy:

   rsync -avz --delete <local-repo> <username>@glimmer.rstudio.com:~/ShinyApps/

On Sat, Apr 20, 2013 at 11:52 AM, Tristan Sloughter <tristan....@gmail.com> wrote:
> Ah ok.
>
> That would be great if you could take care of allowing it to run as non-root. I'm using Shiny at Heroku, so want to be able to run it on our infrastructure :)
>
>
> On Fri, Apr 19, 2013 at 4:37 PM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> > Despite the misleading error message, the problem here is indeed that Shiny Server expects to be run with root privileges.
> >
> > This is because Shiny Server was originally designed to allow all users (or all users in a certain group) on the server to host Shiny apps themselves, and their apps would execute with their permissions. We use su to drop privileges when spawning the R process (rather than simply fork/setuid/exec), since it knows all the subtleties about doing so, e.g. which environment variables need to be dropped/changed, the right incantation to setgid/initgroups, etc.
> >
> > Shiny Server still allows you to do this (it's the autouser <http://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/blob/master/config.html#overview> mode) but with the other two modes of operation, "site directory" (the default) and "direct mapping", it's easy to imagine the Shiny Server process running as a particular user and all the spawned R processes running as the same user. Other than listening on port <1024 there would be no inherent need to run as root. But Shiny Server doesn't detect that case right now.
> >
> > I didn't think about the PaaS case--that is a particularly good reason for us to remove the run-as-root restriction. I'll see if I can take care of this.
> >
> >
> > On Fri, Apr 19, 2013 at 12:35 PM, Tristan Sloughter <tristan....@gmail.com> wrote:
